falklands.overview: The Falkland Islands offer modest but scenic coastal walking across open, windswept ground. The Maritime History Trail runs from Stanley to Cape Pembroke, a short path leads to Magellanic penguins at Gypsy Cove, and a short flight reaches Sea Lion Island, where you can walk freely to wildlife colonies. The best window is October to March.

months.6: Deep cold brings freezing winds and very short daylight hours, reducing walking to brief outings near town.
months.8: Bitter winds continue to sweep the open terrain, keeping the outer island walks largely inaccessible.

months.4: April begins to dry out the lower sheep paths, allowing hikers to tackle the routes. Weather remains highly volatile, and hikers must be prepared for sudden whiteouts or rain squalls on the exposed headlands.
months.8: August keeps the steep trails in their best condition, and the sheer drops to the ocean are breathtaking. Puffins begin to leave the cliffs late in the month, but the long days still provide ample time for long ridge hikes.

fiji.overview: Fiji offers rewarding day hikes through tropical forests and along rugged shorelines. On Taveuni, the Lavena Coastal Walk leads past beaches to a waterfall, requiring a village fee and a rope-assisted creek crossing. On Viti Levu, hikers can tackle the steep trail up the 3,650-foot Mount Batilamu for sweeping island views.

months.1: Heavy rain and cyclone risk make trails like the Lavena Coastal Walk very slippery and sometimes impassable. Heat and humidity are intense.

fjords.overview: The Norwegian Fjords offer some of the most dramatic day hiking in Europe, with trails climbing steeply from the water to sheer cliffs and panoramic ridges. Famous routes include the long, rough hike to Trolltunga, the shorter Preikestolen and Kjeragbolten, and the Besseggen ridge, a classic high-country traverse. The season is short, dictated by snow and daylight, with the high trails only reliably open from midsummer to early fall.

months.6: The main hiking season begins as snow clears from the high routes. Trails to Preikestolen and Kjeragbolten open, though early in the month some snow patches remain.
months.9: A strong month for hiking. The weather cools, and the first autumn snows can dust the highest peaks late in the month.

galapagos.overview: Walking in the Galápagos consists of short, guided excursions to volcanic landscapes and coastal viewpoints rather than independent hiking. Visitors reach the trailheads by boat and follow licensed guides at most sites, along marked paths through lava fields and highland reserves.

gbr.overview: The Great Barrier Reef region offers real walking on its islands, reached by boat or ferry. The best-known route is the Ngaro Track in the Whitsundays, with island day hikes to viewpoints over the turquoise water. The cooler months from May to October are the only sensible time to walk, as tropical heat and humidity make the rest of the year hard going.

months.1: Peak wet season brings intense heat, high humidity and heavy tropical downpours that make island trails muddy.
months.6: Excellent walking conditions with low humidity and cool breezes, perfect for the Ngaro Track.
months.9: Temperatures begin to climb, but the air remains dry enough for comfortable day hikes to the island lookouts.

ghana.overview: Ghana offers modest day hikes built around waterfalls and forest. The standout is the guided hike to the upper tier of Wli Falls, said to be West Africa's tallest waterfall, while Mount Afadjato is a short, steep climb to a summit widely regarded as the country's highest. Kakum National Park has a guided canopy walkway above the rainforest.

months.11: The dry season returns, and trails firm up. The route to Mount Afadjato is open, and the guided hike to the upper Wli Falls reopens once the ground has dried, making this a good time for the steep forest climbs.
months.12: Excellent hiking conditions return with dry trails. The Harmattan winds arrive, bringing dusty haze, but the route to Mount Afadjato is open and the upper Wli Falls hike reopens once the ground has dried.

glacier-waterton.overview: Glacier and Waterton Lakes offer some of the most dramatic alpine hiking in North America, with trails carved into steep sedimentary rock above glacier-carved valleys. Walkers reach the best routes by driving the Going-to-the-Sun Road, taking park shuttles, or crossing lakes by boat. Long day hikes like the Highline Trail and Grinnell Glacier deliver views of jagged peaks and alpine lakes, while Waterton features the steep, cliff-hugging Crypt Lake trail. The high-country season is short, dictated by snowpack and road access.

months.7: The high country is fully accessible, opening routes like the Highline Trail. Walkers traverse steep, rocky ledges above glacier-carved valleys filled with blooming wildflowers.
months.8: Alpine trails are entirely free of snow, offering prime conditions for long day hikes to high passes and glacial lakes.
months.1: Deep snow blankets the parks, closing the high country and the main scenic roads. Walkers can use snowshoes on lower valley routes near the park entrances, passing through snow-covered forests.
months.2: Deep snow blankets the parks, closing the high country and the main scenic roads. Walkers can use snowshoes on lower valley routes near the park entrances, passing through snow-covered forests.
months.12: Deep snow blankets the parks, closing the high country and the main scenic roads. Walkers can use snowshoes on lower valley routes near the park entrances, passing through snow-covered forests.
months.10: The Going-to-the-Sun Road closes by the middle of the month, cutting off access to the high alpine trailheads. Walkers can still enjoy frosty hikes in the lower valleys before heavy snows arrive.

months.3: Spring arrives, melting the ice on the upper trails and bringing ideal hiking weather to the canyon. The inner canyon is warm but not yet dangerous, making this a prime time for steep descents on the Bright Angel and South Kaibab trails.
months.12: Winter conditions return to the South Rim, with snow and ice often covering the upper trails. Traction devices are necessary for descending into the canyon, where the air is crisp.

great-smoky-mountains.overview: The Great Smoky Mountains offer hundreds of miles of trails through dense Appalachian forest to high balds, waterfalls and panoramic ridges. Hikers can climb Alum Cave Trail to Mount LeConte or walk sections of the Appalachian Trail out to Charlie's Bunion, with easy riverside paths, steep rocky ascents and multi-day backcountry treks as well. A parking tag is required for trailheads.

months.5: Excellent hiking conditions arrive with mild temperatures and lush green canopies. The trails are in prime shape for steep climbs up to Mount LeConte.
months.9: Cooler, crisp air returns, making this one of the most comfortable times to tackle long day hikes as the summer heat breaks.

greenland.overview: Greenland offers vast, remote tundra walking, highlighted by the 100-mile Arctic Circle Trail from Kangerlussuaq to Sisimiut. This demanding seven- to ten-day trek requires complete self-sufficiency, passing deep fjords, glacier-carved valleys and inland lakes. Day hikers can walk from coastal towns among icebergs and rugged peaks. The brief walking window runs from June to August.

months.1: Deep snow and harsh cold end hiking; getting around is by dog sled, snowmobile or ski, with only short snowshoe walks near the towns.
months.2: Deep snow and harsh cold end hiking; getting around is by dog sled, snowmobile or ski, with only short snowshoe walks near the towns.

months.12: Deep snow and harsh cold end hiking; getting around is by dog sled, snowmobile or ski, with only short snowshoe walks near the towns.

guatemala.overview: Guatemala is known for its volcano hikes, particularly the strenuous ascents near Antigua. The overnight trek up Acatenango offers views of neighboring Fuego erupting, while Pacaya provides a shorter walk to recent lava flows. Trails around Lake Atitlán connect Maya villages along the steep caldera walls. The dry season from November to April offers the clearest views and safest trail conditions.

months.6: June introduces high heat and humidity, making the steep climbs up the karst peaks hard going, while afternoon rain showers are common.
months.2: February remains cool with occasional drizzle, requiring care on steep limestone stairs, though the riverside trails are atmospheric.

months.4: Temperatures begin to rise, but trails in Topes de Collantes and Viñales remain mostly dry and accessible. Start longer hikes early in the day.
months.8: Peak hurricane risk brings heavy rain and potential trail closures. Mountain routes like Pico Turquino can be closed at short notice.

hokkaido.overview: Hokkaido offers volcanic peaks, caldera lakes and coastal trails that escape the mainland's summer heat. Walkers head to Daisetsuzan National Park for alpine day hikes and multi-day traverses among steaming vents, or to the Shiretoko Peninsula, where brown bears forage and the Five Lakes ground trail needs a permit and bear briefing in bear season. Heavy winter snow keeps the season short.

months.7: Peak summer brings clear trails across Daisetsuzan and the Shiretoko Five Lakes.

hongkong.overview: Hong Kong offers surprisingly extensive walking trails that escape the dense city for green ridges and coastal views. The famous Dragon's Back is a day hike with sweeping ocean panoramas, while the 62-mile MacLehose Trail crosses the New Territories in ten sections. The best conditions arrive late in the year when the air cools.

months.5: Heavy rain and high humidity arrive in May, making the steep climbs hard work and often slippery.
months.9: September brings some relief from the heat, though humidity remains high and early starts are still necessary.

hudson-valley.overview: The Hudson Valley offers a vast network of day hikes, from steep scrambles in the Hudson Highlands to the carriage roads and cliff-edge trails of the Shawangunks. Many trailheads are accessible by a short drive or a direct train from New York City. The walking ranges from easy forest loops to steep rock scrambles like Breakneck Ridge, rewarding hikers with sweeping views of the river and the Catskill foothills.

months.6: Summer brings warm, humid days and lush green forests. Early starts are recommended for steep scrambles like Breakneck Ridge to avoid the midday heat.
months.12: Winter sets in with freezing temperatures and occasional snow. The carriage roads offer easy winter walking, while steep trails become icy and demand careful footing.

ireland.overview: Ireland offers excellent coastal and mountain walking, anchored by long-distance routes like the nine-day Kerry Way and the week-long, 82-mile Wicklow Way. Day hikers can tackle the steep, rocky ascent of Carrauntoohil, the country's highest peak, or explore the rugged cliffs of the west coast. The terrain is famously green and often boggy, with the best conditions arriving in the summer months.

istanbul.overview: Istanbul offers modest but real walking escapes from the city, reached by a short drive or ferry ride. The Princes' Islands have car-free paved and dirt paths with views over the Sea of Marmara, while Belgrad Forest has shaded dirt trails under oak and beech. Spring and fall bring the best walking weather, avoiding the heavy heat of summer and the chill of winter.

months.1: Winter is cool and damp, leaving the dirt trails of Belgrad Forest muddy and the island paths chilly.

jamaica.overview: Jamaica's best walking is anchored by the Blue Mountains, where steep, forested trails lead up to the island's highest point. The classic route is the long day hike to Blue Mountain Peak, often started well before dawn to catch the sunrise and clear views stretching to the coast before the daily clouds roll in. The dry months from December to April offer the most reliable trail conditions.

months.4: The dry season holds on, making this a fine time for the long climb to the peak before heavier rains arrive.
months.6: The rains build, bringing increased humidity and afternoon showers that make early starts essential for any mountain walking.
months.8: High heat and heavy downpours make the mountain trails slick, with storm season at its peak.

jordan.overview: Hiking here means walking among ancient sandstone ruins and vast desert landscapes. At Petra, the steep climb up 800 rock-cut steps to the Monastery earns views over the surrounding valleys, while the back-door trail from Little Petra offers a longer approach along the Jordan Trail. In Wadi Rum, guided desert walks explore towering rock formations and deep canyons. The best walking happens in the mild spring and fall, avoiding the intense summer heat.

joshua-tree.overview: Palm Springs and Joshua Tree offer striking desert hiking, from boulder-strewn landscapes to high alpine ridges. Walkers can explore the palm oases of Indian Canyons or take the aerial tramway to the Mount San Jacinto wilderness for high-elevation trails, where a free permit is required. The season is strictly dictated by the desert heat, making winter the prime time to explore.
